item.text:
**3B.8 Research Note**

**Assessment:** mixed, leaning negative. Peaceful dissent clearly still occurred in 2024, but the best evidence shows Jokowi’s state tolerated it unevenly and sometimes responded with selective detention, internet restrictions, and coercive crowd control, especially in Papua and during the election-law crisis.

**Accepted Claims**
- **Students and activists protest alleged poll interference by Jokowi administration** | **Reuters via ThePrint** | **2024-02-12** | [URL](https://theprint.in/world/indonesia-students-protest-alleged-poll-interference-by-jokowi-administration/1963424/) | Students and activists held public protests accusing Jokowi of abuse of power. This is limited positive evidence that dissent was still possible in public, though it does not prove protection from retaliation. | **3B.8**, **2B.9**
- **Protests across Indonesia as parliament delays change to election law** | **Reuters via Investing.com** | **2024-08-22** | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/protests-across-indonesia-as-parliament-delays-change-to-election-law-3582501) | Reuters reported large protests over the election-law fight, showing that mass dissent remained mobilized. But the same episode also signals an environment where protest was contested and vulnerable to coercive response. | **3B.8**, **2B.9**
- **Freedom on the Net 2024: Indonesia** | **Freedom House** | **2024** | [URL](https://freedomhouse.org/country/indonesia/freedom-net/2024) | Freedom House says Kominfo can directly restrict online content without an appeals process and that connectivity restrictions continued during protests and in Papua. This is strong evidence of arbitrary restrictions and chilling control. | **3B.8**, **3B.5**, **3B.4**, **2B.9**
- **Human Rights Reports: Indonesia** | **U.S. Department of State** | **published 2025-08-12; covers 2024** | [URL](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128570.html) | The report says police temporarily detained critics and peaceful demonstrators, especially in Papua, and that the state did not systematically investigate abuses. This supports a negative finding on retaliation-free protest and dissent. | **3B.8**, **3B.2**, **3B.4**, **2B.9**
- **Protests across Indonesia as parliament delays change to election law** | **Reuters via Investing.com** | **2024-08-22** | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/protests-across-indonesia-as-parliament-delays-change-to-election-law-3582501) | Reuters reported security forces used tear gas and water cannon against protesters during the election-law crisis. That is evidence of coercive crowd control rather than clean tolerance of dissent. | **3B.8**, **3B.2**, **3B.5**
- **Annual Overview 2024** | **Papuans Behind Bars** | **2025-07-23; covers 2024** | [URL](https://papuansbehindbars.org/annual-overview-2024/) | The overview recorded 370 political arrests in 2024, with most detainees released within hours or days. This suggests repeated short-term intimidation of political activity, even if it was not always prolonged imprisonment. | **3B.8**, **3B.2**, **2B.9**

**Search Gap**
- I did **not** find strong evidence that Jokowi built a durable pro-dissent architecture protecting protests, community groups, and critics from retaliation.
- I also did **not** find evidence of a nationwide shutdown of protest rights or a full ban on civil society.
- The record is therefore best read as **some protest space remained, but it was narrowed by selective detention, internet restrictions, and coercive policing**, especially in Papua.
